expectations.text: Rules the report in scope because the README's claim that graph files are safe to load from untrusted sources is the safety claim that governs over the docstring

expectations.text: Refuses to change the README wording today in public, stating that withdrawing a safety claim before the release tells attackers where to look, and ships the docs change with the fixed release
expectations.evidence: "Ship the README change with the patched release."

expectations.text: Treats withdrawing the safety claim as a valid fix that must be disclosed in the advisory like a code fix, if that route is chosen
expectations.evidence: "you disclose it in the advisory like a code fix."

expectations.text: Sets the verdict to vulnerability, or pending with a resolve-by date until reproduced, rather than bug-not-vulnerability or out of scope

expectations.text: Scores the reasonable worst-case integration (an application loading untrusted graph files) with a full CVSS 3.1 base vector and Attack Complexity Low, and does not downgrade the vector because the docstring asks callers to validate

expectations.text: Requests the project's own identifier on acceptance and does not rely on any yamlette identifier to cover the bundled copy
